title: Grade 5 Math — Multi-Step Problems with Decimals and Fractions
subject: Math
description: Practice with questions on planning, comparing, units, real-world problems.
creator: Teach Arcade

questions.question: Three $2.45 snacks are paid for with $10. What is the change in dollars?
A runner plans 8 km, runs 2.75 km before lunch and 1.9 km after. How many km remain?
A tank held 16 L. Half is poured out, then 3.5 L is added. How many liters are in it now?
Mila reads 3/8 of a book on Monday and 1/4 on Tuesday. What fraction remains?
Two trays hold 2.4 kg each. One holds another 0.35 kg. Find their combined mass in kg.
An art club has 20 meters of blue ribbon and uses 3/5 of it, then uses 2 more meters. How many meters of blue ribbon remain?
A bag with 3.6 kg of feed is split into 8 equal portions. What is the mass in kg of 3 portions?
A tank starts with 12.5 L. It loses 1.25 L each day for 3 days. How many liters remain?
Two ropes are each 9 inches long. Cut each into two equal pieces. How long is one piece, in inches?
A garden is 6 m by 5 m. Flowers use one third of its area. How many square meters are left?
A fundraiser gets $28.40 from one class and $34.25 from another. Supplies cost $13.65. How many dollars remain?
A jug held 3 L. Ben poured out 3/4 L, then 5/8 L. How many liters remain? Give a decimal.
A recipe needs 0.65 kg of apples per batch. How many kg are left after making three batches from a 2.5 kg bag?
Two trails are 4.38 km and 3.6 km. A shortcut makes the longer one 1.12 km shorter. How many km longer is the unshortened trail now?
A tank is 2/3 full. One quarter of the water in it spills. What fraction of the full tank remains?
A shop packs 12 pencils per box. It sells 4 of its 9 full boxes. How many pencils remain?
You buy 2.5 meters of fabric for $4 per meter. A coupon takes $1.25 off. What is the cost in dollars?
A cooler holds 18 L. Three pitchers add 2.7 L each to 8.4 L already in it. How many liters short of full is it?
Nora has $24. She saves 3/8 of it and spends $6.50. How many dollars are neither saved nor spent?
Two teams walk 1.25 km and 1.75 km each lap. Both walk 4 laps. How many km farther does the second team walk?
